prompt: Why did no capture in this course ever place an ordinary pod on `shop-control-plane`?

choices.why: All three nodes report the same allocatable.
Right: `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane`, set by kubeadm.

choices.text: The scheduler skips the first node
choices.why: There is no such rule.

prompt: A Deployment tolerates `dedicated=reports:NoSchedule` but has no `nodeSelector`. Where can its pods land?
hint: A toleration permits; it does not direct.

choices.why: That needs a selector or affinity as well.

choices.text: Nowhere, until a selector is added
choices.why: Untainted nodes accept it as they accept any pod.
Right. The tainted one becomes allowed, not chosen.

choices.text: Only on nodes with no taint
choices.why: The toleration makes the tainted node allowed too.

prompt: `shop-worker` got `maintenance=now:NoExecute`. What happened to the four shop pods running on it?

choices.why: That would be `NoSchedule`.
Pods never move, and that node was reserved.
Kubernetes has no paused pods.

choices.text: They were evicted, and replacements stayed `Pending`
choices.why: Right. No node could take them.

prompt: Every pod tolerates `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute` for 300 seconds by default. What does that number decide?
hint: Who sets that taint, and when?

choices.text: How long before a lost node's pods are replaced
choices.why: Right. Kubernetes taints the node itself; after 300 s the pods are evicted.

choices.text: How long a pod may run in total
choices.why: Tolerations do not limit a healthy node.
Probes are separate settings.
That is the kubelet's own setting.
